name: Media generation
description: Let the chat model make a picture, a voice-over or a clip while it works.
long_description:
A chat model can draw. Not itself — it calls a model built for it, the way it calls any other tool, and what comes back appears in the reply at the point it asked for it.

This is the other direction from picking an image model in the model dialog. There, the image model is who you are talking to and it answers with a picture instead of words. Here you keep talking to the chat model, and a picture is one step of its work: it can describe what it is about to make, make it, and then write about what it made.

One call makes one thing. There is no batch and no `n`: a model that wants three pictures calls three times, and each call is one charge you can see on the card. It uses the models your own provider keys reach, at your own account's prices, and the result says which model was used and what it cost.

It writes nothing to this machine. The file lives in the chat, the way an attachment does.

risk.notes: Every call spends money on the provider account whose key you added — a picture is cents, a clip can be a dollar or more. It asks before each generation outside Auto, and the card names the model. Nothing is written to this machine: what it makes lives in the chat.

DEFAULT_IMAGE_MODEL.title: Default model for a picture
DEFAULT_IMAGE_MODEL.description: What a call uses when it does not name a model. The options are the models your own provider keys reach, newest first; ones over a year old are marked, and this menu is the only place one of those can be chosen.

DEFAULT_SPEECH_MODEL.title: Default model for spoken audio
DEFAULT_SPEECH_MODEL.description: The same, for anything read aloud.

DEFAULT_VIDEO_MODEL.title: Default model for a video clip
DEFAULT_VIDEO_MODEL.description: The same, for clips. These are the expensive ones.

DEFAULT_MODEL_RULE.title: When those defaults apply
DEFAULT_MODEL_RULE.description: A chat model may name a model of its own. This is how much notice to take of it: only when it names none, that plus every call in Auto where no card asks you anything, or always.

prompt.system_addendum: media__generate makes one picture, one piece of spoken audio, or one video clip, and it appears in your reply at the point you called it. Write about the thing itself; never describe it as a link, a file path or an attachment, and never claim to have looked at it afterwards — you cannot read it back. Call it once per thing: a second picture is a second call, and each one costs the user money, so do not make one nobody asked for, and do not regenerate to "improve" something unless you were asked to. A diagram is an artifact, not an image: use gantry__create_artifact with the mermaid type for anything with boxes and arrows. Do not guess a model id: leave `model` out and the user's own default answers, or call media__list_models first — it is free, it reads a local list, and it is the only place the real ids are. Models over a year old are not yours to pick at all. The result of a generation says which model answered and what it cost.
